WPT|/rc.adv.label: Advantages
WPT|/rc.adv.title: Why the system works
WPT|/rc.adv.cards/0/2: The water becomes the transport medium
WPT|/rc.adv.cards/0/3: The active ingredients of {IC} penetrate the concrete through its capillaries; water entering the component carries them deeper. They react to insoluble crystals that fill the smallest pores and cracks — and go on doing so whenever water arrives.
WPT|/rc.adv.cards/1/2: From the inside, against pressing water
WPT|/rc.adv.cards/1/3: {IC} is watertight against negative pressing water up to 1.5 bar; {IM} is suitable for negative water pressure. Basements, pits and tanks are sealed from the accessible side, without excavation.
WPT|/rc.adv.cards/2/3: CRD-C 48-92: 14 bar. Under EN 1504-2 (principle 2.2, moisture control) the capillary water absorption is w < 0.1 kg/m²·h⁰·⁵ while the coating stays vapour permeable (class I, sD < 5 m).
WPT|/rc.adv.cards/3/3: Hairline cracks that open after the application are sealed by renewed crystal growth ({IC} increased active crack healing). Static cracks and joints wider than 0.4 mm are opened 20 × 25 mm and filled with {IM}.
WPT|/rc.adv.cards/4/3: {IC} is suitable for drinking water containers; the tank is rinsed thoroughly with drinking water before it is filled. Filling of containers is possible after 3 days.
WPT|/rc.adv.cards/5/3: {F20} solidifies after 1–2 minutes, even under water, with a strong bond to concrete and no corrosion-promoting substances: approx. 3 N/mm² after 1 hour, approx. 30 N/mm² after 28 days.
WPT|/rc.pictos/0/2: {IC}, {IM} and {F20}: pre-blended dry mortars, mixed with water on site
WPT|/rc.pictos/1/2: DIN EN 1504-2 with Declaration of Performance, CRD-C 48-92, DVGW worksheets W 270 and W 347, reaction to fire A1
WPT|/rc.pictos/2/2: chloride-free, carbonation reducing, can be applied to damp substrates

WPT|/rc.rel.sub: Where crystalline waterproofing meets the mineral slurries, restoration and injection.
WPT|/rc.rel.rows/0/1: The rigid and flexible slurries for the classic build-up with a sealing cove: {AQ1K}, {AQ2K}, {RB400} — where the waterproofing may be plastered, tiled or painted over.
WPT|/rc.rel.rows/1/1: Voids and honeycombs are re-profiled before the crystalline slurry goes on: bond coat {HSF}, repair mortar {BIS540}, fine smoothing mortar {BIS16}; {IM} where water is involved.
WPT|/rc.rel.rows/2/1: Moving cracks are not filled with mortar: they are injected with {P1}, {P4} or {IH} before the surface is waterproofed.

WPT|/rc.m3d.microNote: Micro scale: schematic close-up of a sectioned sample at the coating interface, not to scale. Each stage plays as a short animation.
WPT|/rc.m3d.microSub/rctank: Micro scale shows the interface itself: the pores and a fine crack of the concrete skin, the two coats of {IC} on it, and the crystals growing from the coating into the pores and the crack until the water standing on the finished tank can no longer enter.
WPT|/rc.m3d.microSub/rcwall: Micro scale shows the jetted concrete skin, water pressing into the pores and the crack from the rear, the two coats of {IC} — and the crystals that grow into the capillaries and the crack and hold the water back (negative side, up to 1.5 bar).
WPT|/rc.m3d.microSub/rcpit: Micro scale shows the concrete skin of the pit with water pressing from the rear, the two coats of {IC}, and the crystals filling the capillaries and the crack until the pit stays dry.
WPT|/rc.m3d.microSub/rcsew: Micro scale shows the concrete skin of the tank, the two coats of {IC}, and the crystals growing into the pores and the crack — the sealed pore structure keeps the aggressive water out of the concrete.
WPT|/rc.m3d.co/rctank/0/0: Made good before it is coated
WPT|/rc.m3d.co/rctank/0/1: Water jetting at > 400 bar lays the concrete bare; static cracks over 0.4 mm are chased 20 × 25 mm, their edges screened with {IC} and filled flush with {IM}; the coved fillet of approx. 4 cm follows wet in wet.
WPT|/rc.m3d.co/rctank/1/0: Two coats into the damp concrete
WPT|/rc.m3d.co/rctank/1/1: {IC} is brushed evenly into the repeatedly wetted, matt damp substrate; the second coat while the first is still sticky; 1.5 kg/m² for accumulated water. It can be sprayed (Technical Information No. 43).
WPT|/rc.m3d.co/rctank/2/1: Protected from sun and wind for ≥ 24 hours, kept damp for ≥ 3 days from the day after application; filling possible after 3 days, drinking water tanks rinsed first. Pressurised water after ≥ 7 days; up to a month to the full sealing effect.
WPT|/rc.m3d.co/rcwall/0/1: Where water runs through the joint the opening is chiselled to a dovetail and a plug of {F20} is pressed in by hand until it hardens — after 1–2 minutes, with a noticeable warming, even under water.
WPT|/rc.m3d.co/rcwall/1/1: The construction joint and the cracks are chased 20 × 25 mm, screened with {IC} and filled flush with {IM}; the coved fillet of approx. 4 cm on a screen of {IC}; {IC} over the fresh mortar after 1–3 hours.
